messages:
alex: FYI noticed a ~20% p99 increase on host decode path after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. looks host-side parsing/tokenization + grpc writev are up. flamegraph attached in my follow-up snapshot.

maria: Oof. Is this across all models or only long-context jobs? :thinking:

alex: Mostly long-context (>= 1024). short requests not affected. perf shows more time in `TokenStream::next` and `grpc::Writev` syscall overheads. also seeing extra small fragments from the framer.

devon: Can you paste the perf snippet? curious if it's contention (locks) or syscall churn.

alex: paste of pprof stack sample (top lines):
```
# pprof sample
40%  host_process  TokenStream::next
18%  host_process  parse::deserialize_frame
12%  libc          writev
8%   host_process  kv_cache::lookup (miss path)
5%   host_process  Buffer::append (alloc)
```

alex: also saw many `writev` calls with tiny iovecs (~200-800 bytes) from streaming chunker. causes socket syscall ratio to tokens generated to go way up.

jin: That's the classic fragmentation problem. Did the kernel selection change batch layout for decoder so streaming pieces are smaller?

alex: yeah, the kernel change altered output chunk boundaries slightly — more frequent flushes on partial decode paths. when combined with the streaming framer we end up sending N small frames instead of one coalesced frame.

kartik: Is KV cache thrashing related or separate? you mentioned lookup misses.

alex: related-ish. kv cache lookups are more likely on mid-sequence tokens because batching heuristics changed: micro-batches are split earlier, so some requests lose the prefix cache hit chance — more backend work -> longer token latency -> more streaming slices -> more writev. vicious cycle.

maria: Any quick mitigations we can A/B?

devon: A few quick ideas: reduce flush frequency in framer for small writes; add a socket coalescing layer that buffers up to X ms or Y bytes; bump micro-batch cut threshold to favor slightly larger batches; tune kernel selection to prefer same-boundary behavior for long contexts.

alex: tried a prototype: framer coalesce 4ms or 4KB whichever earlier. microbench on staging: p99 host decode down from 210ms -> 165ms, system writev syscalls -62%, cpu off-host down ~12%. no functional regressions.

jin: Nice. Any downsides? added latency for first token?

alex: first token median increased by ~6ms on streaming cold-starts. acceptable for our SLOs but we should surface flag for latency-sensitive routes.

kartik: For KV cache: maybe adjust batching window so prefix chunking stays aligned. Could also add a cheap heuristic: if seq_len > threshold, prefer batch variant that preserves prefix grouping.

maria: Can we make this config-driven per-route so embedded search (latency sensitive) vs chat (throughput) get different defaults?

devon: yes, expose `stream.coalesce_ms`, `stream.coalesce_bytes`, `batching.min_effective_tokens` as per-route config. default = 0/0 and 1. staging configs for long-context workloads we set coalesce_ms=4, coalesce_bytes=4096, batching.min_effective_tokens=32.

alex: i'll push the framer patch to a feature branch and run full perf sweep. plan: run canary for 24h on 10% traffic, watch token-level cost and p99. If stable, roll to 50%.

maria: Also add metrics: `host.writev.count_small`, `host.writev.iov_avg`, `kv.cache.hit_rate_by_seq_bucket`, and `stream.first_token.latency` so we can monitor regressions automatically.

jin: Good. One more: check HPACK/HTTP2 header pressure — small frames + many headers can blow CPU. if we see header churn, consider persistent header contexts or header compression tuning.

alex: noted. running a full trace now (flamegraphs, eBPF syscalls). will post results. thanks all :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-457 - host decode p99 regression. linked to this thread.

maria: Great. if the canary looks good, we should document the default coalescing behavior in runtime docs and add a short explainer in the console rollout notes.

devon: Also add an automated test that simulates long-context streaming and asserts writev syscall count per token stays under threshold. helps prevent accidental kernel changes from regressing this again.

alex: Will do. posting branch and perf logs in ~30m.
